transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Okay, I think most people are on. Lukas said he'd be a few minutes late, so we'll do legs and arms first and pick structures up when he joins.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Sounds good. Let's keep it tight today, I have a hard stop.

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Understood. So, first, legs. Priya, where are we?

transcript.speaker: p-priya
transcript.text: Where are we on legs. So, um, three things. One, the knee joint life test is still running clean, Dmitri can speak to the details. Two, we found a clearance issue between the shin cover and the harness at full flexion. Three, the foot sole bonding is giving us some voids, which we're looking at with the techs.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: How bad is the clearance issue?

transcript.speaker: p-priya
transcript.text: It's rubbing, not pinching. I'd rather fix it now than find it as a chafed wire in a month. It's a cover change, not a structural one.

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: Life test is fine. Rig one had encoder drift, Lin reseated the connector, it's back up.

transcript.speaker: p-jonas
transcript.text: was that the drift that tripped the fault log

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: p-jonas
transcript.text: ok

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Okay. Sofia, arms and hands.

transcript.speaker: p-sofia
transcript.text: Finger tendon routing rev is done and the first hand is reassembled. Grip force is better but the pinky still lags the others. I think it's friction in the sheath, not the motor.

transcript.speaker: p-farah
transcript.text: Is that the same motor driver as the index finger?

transcript.speaker: p-sofia
transcript.text: Same driver, same firmware. That's why I'm blaming the sheath.

transcript.speaker: p-jonas
transcript.text: i can pull current traces if you want to rule it out

transcript.speaker: p-sofia
transcript.text: Yes please, that would help.

transcript.speaker: p-lukas
transcript.text: hey sorry, back to back

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: No problem, you're right on time actually. Structures.

transcript.speaker: p-lukas
transcript.text: pelvis casting review done, two comments on draft angle, nothing blocking

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Did the vendor push back on the wall thickness?

transcript.speaker: p-lukas
transcript.text: no they took it

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Great. Farah, electrical.

transcript.speaker: p-farah
transcript.text: Electrical. So, one, the battery management board rev is back and bring-up is mostly done; two, we had one brownout on the hip axis during a fast squat, which I think is a harness drop more than the supply; three, I'd like to get the harness team and Priya together about the shin routing because that's the same bundle.

transcript.speaker: p-priya
transcript.text: Yes, let's do that this week.

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: the brownout, was that with the new current limits or the old ones

transcript.speaker: p-farah
transcript.text: New ones. Jonas pushed them last week.

transcript.speaker: p-jonas
transcript.text: yep

transcript.speaker: p-omar
transcript.text: Quick one on test capacity, I think we're probably going to be short on dyno time if the actuator work and the life test both need it the same week. Not 100% sure, I need to look at the schedule again.

transcript.speaker: p-dmitri
transcript.text: We will be short. Plan for it.

transcript.speaker: p-omar
transcript.text: Okay, I'll put together a dyno calendar and send it around.

transcript.speaker: p-nora
transcript.text: On manufacturing, you're asking where the builds stand. So, one, kitting for the next leg build is mostly complete, we're short a handful of fasteners that are on order; two, the assembly travelers are updated; three, I'd like one more dry run of the knee subassembly before the real build.

transcript.speaker: p-gwen
transcript.text: Fasteners should be fine, they're stock items. The longer lead stuff is what I'm watching.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Let's do the dry run. Cheap insurance.

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Okay, schedule. I'll go through the changes since last week. First, the Leg DVT build has moved. It's now 11/4. The kitting and the dry run Nora mentioned feed into that.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Okay. Anything downstream I should worry about?

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Anything downstream? I'm checking that now, I'll have it by the next review.

transcript.speaker: p-priya
transcript.text: Honestly the slack helps us with the shin cover change.

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: on actuators, the dyno runs on the new rotor are going ok, back emf matches the model within noise. still chasing a little cogging at low speed

transcript.speaker: p-jonas
transcript.text: is that cogging or the encoder interpolation

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: probably encoder honestly, i want to swap it and rerun thurs. well, fri more likely

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Second schedule change. Hip actuator thermal derate at continuous torque has moved to 10/12.

transcript.speaker: p-arjun
transcript.text: ok. we'll need the dyno for that one

transcript.speaker: p-omar
transcript.text: Right, I'll make sure it's on the calendar I think.

transcript.speaker: p-beth
transcript.text: Okay. Last thing, I'll send the updated milestone list out after this, please flag anything I've got wrong.

transcript.speaker: p-ingrid
transcript.text: Thanks everyone. I've got to jump.

summary.overview: Weekly hardware program review covering legs, arms and hands, structures, electrical, manufacturing, actuators and schedule. Lukas joined late. Two schedule changes were noted: the Leg DVT build is now 11/4 and Hip actuator thermal derate at continuous torque is now 10/12.
shorthand_bullet: Legs: knee life test running; shin cover rubs harness at full flexion, cover change only; sole bonding voids
Arms/hands: tendon routing rev done, pinky lags, suspect sheath friction
Structures: pelvis casting review done, minor draft angle comments
Electrical: BMS board bring-up mostly done; one hip brownout on fast squat, likely harness drop
Dyno capacity likely short when actuator work overlaps life test
Manufacturing: kitting mostly complete, travelers updated, one more knee dry run
Actuators: back EMF matches model, low-speed cogging maybe encoder
Hip actuator thermal derate at continuous torque moved to 10/12

Omar to build and circulate a dyno calendar
Nora to schedule knee subassembly dry run
Beth to check downstream impact of Leg DVT build change
Beth to send updated milestone list
Arjun to swap encoder and rerun dyno
